The right-hand triple fireball is spawned with flags $0300 where the left-hand one uses $0200 (the hidden bit $0100 of $16 would make it not count as a hit source): OQ-I037-13. The death of Poseidon (HP 0) and the release of the King (lair $103) are handled by the engine, not by this script; no code here ends the fight.
player_core:
The player: spawn script, input filter, action choice, per-frame motion finish, push zones, corner slide, Gem pull and return-trip facing, together with the 28 pose handlers, the four swings, PayPhoenixCost, PublishPlayerAnim and the four Phoenix projectiles (file offsets 5394-8143 and 9848-9959, SNES $00:9512-$9FCF and $00:A678-$A6E7, bank 00). The blade layer, soul orb, spells and level-up of the same hero are in player_spells_level_up.

=== ONE ACTOR, FIVE HELPERS ===
The hero is one actor per scene, created from the first record of the world's meta table (WorldMetaPointers: seven identical entries with animation 0, $16 = $1180, animation table PlayerAnims and the script InitPlayerActor). InitPlayerActor stores its slot in player_actor, selects the sprite tile source $7F:3000 (COP A9) and clones five helpers, each of which starts as a copy of the player: WatchForLevelUp (COP 84), RunSoulOrb (84; it spawns RunSoulOrbController), FilterPlayerInput (84), FinishPlayerMove (85) and RunWeaponLayer (85). Run order inside a frame: WatchForLevelUp, RunSoulOrb, RunSoulOrbController, FilterPlayerInput, the player, RunWeaponLayer, FinishPlayerMove. So the controller reads joy_pressed before the filter strips B and Y (spells work without a weapon), and it sees the position that FinishPlayerMove published in the previous frame.
With return_active set (the scene is entered from a stored return point: return_area, return_scene, return_x, return_y and the switch record return_record) InitPlayerActor spawns only the level-up watcher and the hero becomes FacePlayerTowardReturnTarget: no orb, filter, weapon layer or camera follow. Every scene load builds the full set again.

=== ANIMATION STEPS, NOT FRAMES ===
An actor script resumes when its countdown $14 underflows. COP 82 steps the animation and the actor yields for the step duration plus one frame; the engine applies the step velocity ($04 dx, $06 dy) every frame. So the player script runs once per animation step, not once per frame: a walk cycle is six steps, and the first step of every walk handler moves 2 px per frame in all four directions (static reading, OQ-I032-15). The idle animations $00-$03 are one step of duration 0, so while the hero stands the script runs every frame and decides again at once. Whatever has to react between two steps (a released key, the sword button) must cut in from outside: that is the job of FilterPlayerInput, which writes ChoosePlayerAction into the resume pointer $18.
Direction codes are the game's own: 0 up, 1 down, 2 right, 3 left for the facing (PlayerFacingByAnim) and for the movement direction (PlayerMoveDirByAnim). The idle animations $00-$03 are the poses facing down, up, left, right.

=== CHOOSING THE ACTION ===
ChoosePlayerAction runs after every animation. A dying hero ($16 bit $0400) goes to PlayPlayerDeath. With no weapon or in a no-combat scene the unarmed path is used, otherwise the armed path. Plain walking is a direct branch (Right, Left, Down, Up in that priority; BRL StartWalkRight and so on). Everything else goes through PlayerActionTable: 44 rows (one per animation $00-$2B) of 6 handler addresses, slot 0 = B (armed only), 1 = Right, 2 = Left, 3 = Down, 4 = Up, 5 = no key. The table path is taken when L or R is held, when B is held (armed), or when no direction is held (idle).
The rows depend only on the facing of the current animation, except the twelve rows $14-$1F (all StartIdleUp). So the table says: keep the facing, choose the pose of the pressed key. With L or R held the hero keeps his facing, which is the crab-walk of the walkthrough (02-grass-valley.md: 'press and hold the L or R Button to basically move sideways', with a sword also a thrust). Pressing a direction without L or R turns him that way.
The carry on entry to a handler picks between the two animation ids of the paired handlers: clear = pose family $00-$13 (unarmed, or armed with L or R held: the thrust, the blade stays out); set = armed without L or R, pose family $24-$2B (sword carried). The sword hurts only while the animation is below $24 (ApplySwordHit).

=== MOTION ===
FinishPlayerMove runs after the player: the push of a conveyor or wind (ScanPushZones reads an 8-byte record list: x0, x1, y0, y1 tile bounds, dx and dy words in pixels per frame, a first byte of $FF ends the list; 13 lists and 54 records in the game, 52 of them move 1 px per frame and two in St. Elles 4 px), else the corner slide, an even-pixel snap, the published position, the blade layer and the camera. The conveyor belts are in Grass Valley (walkthrough chapter 2), the wind in Magridd's Castle (chapter 7: 'the wind on the ship will be pushing you back').
SlideAroundCorner lets the hero slide 2 px along a wall into a gap when his key is held and he is not tile aligned on the other axis. PullGemsToPlayer pulls Gems toward a hero who stands still with the sword out and L or R held (the thrust idle).

=== NOTES ===
- Walkthrough: crab-walk and thrust with L or R (chapters 1 and 2), the minimum level of a weapon applies to the B swing but not to thrusts (items.md), conveyor belts (chapter 2) and ship wind (chapter 7). The walkthrough does not name the hero (you choose a name), so the notes say 'the hero'.
- An earlier reading called PullGemsToPlayer a 'sword push-back scan'; the code moves pickups toward the hero and touches no enemy (OQ-I032-1).
- Dead or unexplained: SlideUnusedReturn is an unreferenced RTS; AnimKeepKeyMask words $14-$23 are never read; animations $14-$1B and $1D-$1F are protected by the filter but nothing identified plays them (OQ-I032-2).
- Bank limits: every JSR inside the file is a 2-byte reference, so the filter, motion and Gem routines must stay in bank 00 with their callees; PlayerActionTable holds 2-byte handler addresses, so the table and the handlers share bank 00.
player_spells_level_up:
The hero's blade layer, soul orb, magic and level-up: RunWeaponLayer, RunSoulOrb and RunSoulOrbController, the spell gate DispatchSpellCast, the seven spells with their child actors, EndSpellActor and the level-up watcher with its 'LEVEL UP !' blink (file offsets 8143-9848, 9959-9971 and 12118-12293, SNES $00:9FCF-$A678, $00:A6E7-$A6F3 and $00:AF56-$B005, bank 00; the four Phoenix projectiles between them belong to player_core). All of it is spawned by InitPlayerActor.

=== BLADE LAYER AND SOUL ORB ===
RunWeaponLayer is a clone of the player with $16 and $CEFF (visible, no tile collision, not-a-hit-source bit cleared) and the animation bank $0B changed to $0C, so it plays the blade sprites of WeaponOverlayAnims while the body plays PlayerAnims. FinishPlayerMove puts it on the player every frame.
RunSoulOrb stays hidden ($16 bit $2000) while return_active is set or souls_flags is 0, then shows the orb: the walkthrough says the Soul of Magician 'also ends up being the little orb of light surrounding you'. It spawns RunSoulOrbController, which moves an invisible steering point and writes the orb's position every frame: the d-pad moves the point 2 px per frame per axis whether or not the hero can move, a pull toward the hero adds 1 px (2 px at 80 px or more distance to the right or below, 96 px to the left, 64 px above), and the orb sits on a circle of radius 31 px around the point (the sine tables SineTable and SineTableTail, index soul_orbit_phase x 2 mod 256, sample / 4, so 128 phases per turn at one phase per frame). The orb can be parked in front of enemies; spells start at the orb. The walkthrough: a soul reveals hidden passages in King Magridd's Castle 'as your orb of light circles over them'.

=== SPELLS ===
DispatchSpellCast is called by the controller every frame. With no spell alive and Y pressed, equipped_magic - $11 picks the arm; each arm pays with COP 26 (BCD Gems, halved by Magic Armor, zero with the Magic Bell; too poor: nothing is cast), increments spell_active_count and spawns the cast actor with COP 85.
equipped_magic: spell (ROM text and walkthrough magic.md agree), Gems, cast actor, damage byte $30 of the projectile (ApplyProjectileHit reads it):
$11 Flame Ball, 4 Gems, RunFlameBall, 5. $12 Light Arrow, 8, RunLightArrow (four arrows), 10 each. $13 Magic Flair, 8, RunMagicFlair, 20. $14 Rotator, 1 per burst, RunRotator, 5 per burst. $15 Spark Bomb, 8, RunSparkBombSpawner (four bombs), 30 each. $16 Flame Pillar, 20, RunFlamePillarSpawner (four pillars), 6. $17 Tornado, 8, RunTornado, 15. $18 Phoenix, 2, not here: the sword swings cast it (PayPhoenixCost).
Every cast actor copies the orb's position at its first run and plays animations of bank $0F (COP A8 #$8000, #$0F = MagicAnims); the movement is in the animation steps (velocity words per step), not in the scripts. $16 values: $03A0 = harmless while it forms (projectile $0020, not a hit target $0200, not yet a hit source $0100), $02A0 = armed (bit $0100 cleared), $2020 = hidden projectile of a spawner, $0010 added = runs in sub-frames. The Flame Ball goes in the facing direction (PlayerFacingByAnim; the opposite directions use the flip commands COP 96 and 98), the Light Arrow in all four, Magic Flair is charged by holding Y (tap plus three levels: animations $0D/$10, $0E/$11, $0E/$12, $0E/$13), the Rotator releases a burst every 5 frames while Y is held, the Spark Bomb and Flame Pillar spawners drop four actors about 18 frames apart, and the Tornado wanders in a four-state heading graph (see RunTornado).

=== THE CAST LOCK ===
spell_active_count counts the live spell actors and is tested first by the gate, so no spell at all can be cast while one lives (the walkthrough only says one Tornado is allowed: OQ-I032-7). The Flame Ball, Light Arrow, Magic Flair and Rotator actors end through EndSpellActor, which clears the count and consumes the Y press (TRB $4000 of joy_release_latch: a held Y does not cast again); the Flame Ball clears the count already at the launch. The Spark Bomb, Flame Pillar and Tornado parents reset the count to 0 and let their children INC / DEC it; the last one to end consumes the press. The gate also refuses when the free actor stack ($4A) is empty.

=== LEVEL UP ===
WatchForLevelUp loads the EXP needed for the next level from LevelExpThresholds[player_level x 4] (two big-endian BCD words, the first one is the high word) and compares it with player_exp as a 32-bit subtract. At 50 it ends. On a level: max HP and HP + 2 capped at 100, COP 37 refills the bar over time, player_level and player_level_bcd + 1, the new level's low bit chooses level_defense (odd) or level_power (even) + 1, the HUD is marked dirty, BRK #$97, then 'LEVEL UP !' (LevelUpText) is printed three times for 21 frames each with 11 frames of blank (LevelUpClearText) between, and the watcher checks again, so a big EXP gain gives several levels in a row.

=== NOTES ===
- Walkthrough checks: the seven Gem costs, the four-arrow Light Arrow, the three charge levels of Magic Flair, one Tornado, the Rotator's 1 Gem per burst, the level cap of 50, max HP + 2 per level (8 at level 1, 100 at level 47), strength at even and defense at odd levels, and four EXP table rows (level 1 = 100, level 2 = 280, level 18 = 83,000, level 19 = 115,000) agree with the code. The ROM spells the third spell 'Magic Flair' as the walkthrough does.
- DISCREPANCY, Spark Bomb: the walkthrough says four bombs at sixty-degree intervals, the fourth 180 degrees from the first; the code spaces them about 18 frames apart at 2 of 256 sine steps per frame, about 51 degrees each (OQ-I032-3).
- DISCREPANCY, strength and defense: the walkthrough caps the unequipped values at 13 and 12; level_power and level_defense have no cap here, and lib_menus clamps only the display of the level parts to 12 (OQ-I032-8).
- The Tornado's first heading and every restart use LDA #$0302, an immediate that is always 2 (OQ-I032-6).

shared_actor_helpers_bank0:
The shared actor helpers of bank 00: a colour-cycle loop, the flight of the enemy aimed shot and the Master of the shrines (file offsets 10728-10731, 11623-11967 and 30316-31318, SNES $00:A9E8-$A9EB, $00:AD67-$AEBF and $00:F66C-$FA56; bank 00).

=== WHAT RUNS HERE ===
- cm_fx_palette_cycle_loop_0029E8: the one-command script of the 65 meta entries that only cycle palette entries (COP 94 every frame over a colour list of PaletteAnimLists).
- cm_enemy_aimed_shot_body_002D67 and cm_enemy_aimed_shot_mover_002D96: the flight of an enemy shot. Eight shot scripts (the Blue Torch, Fire Man and Fire Bat fireballs, the statues of the castle dungeon and the towers, the Bouncing Ball, the pop-up turret of the World of Evil, the Tin Doll) set Y to their flight animation, push the address of the body and RTL into it. The body spawns the invisible mover just before the shot (COP 85); the mover fixes a direction once, from the hero's position at that moment, and drags the shot along a straight line. The Purple Flower's bee (gw_lostside_marsh_enemies) spawns the mover on its own.
- cm_npc_master_*: the Master of the shrine scenes of Up Above (A00S01-A00S07, one meta type per world: $55, $4C, $51, $3D, $2D, $36, $10; flags $2040). He has no sprite and speaks as 'A voice came from above' (the ROM never names him; the walkthrough calls him the Master). The walkthrough: the northern square of Up Above 'will allow you to save your adventure, as well as move on later in the game' (01-in-the-beginning.md), and the shrine fully restores the hero's health on arrival.

=== HOW THE MASTER WORKS ===
The root heals the hero (COP 37) and falls into the poll loop, which every frame tests the hero's tile (COP 0D with slot 0): tile (7,4) opens the menu, tile (7,6) is the arrival tile (comfort after a death, then the one-time stone hint). The menu is Record / Quit, or Record / Move / Quit once event flag $1B00 is set. WorldMetaPointers:
Actor meta tables: the 7-word world pointer table and the seven lists of 14-byte actor types, 469 entries in all (file offsets 32768-39347, SNES $01:8000-$99B3, bank 00; 6580 bytes).

=== MODEL ===
Every actor placed in a scene, every lair monster and the player is an instance of a meta type: one 14-byte row that gives its stats, first animation, animation table and script. There is one list per world (world_index 0-6: Grass Valley, GreenWood, St. Elles, Mountain of Souls, Leo's Laboratory, Magridd's Castle, World of Evil), so a type number means something different in each world: type $1F is the Metal Mantis in world 0 and a Mini Race Car in world 4. SpawnSceneActors stores the offset of the world's list in $03B0; every consumer reads its row at WorldMetaPointers + $03B0 + type x 14 (listings show $&WorldMetaPointers+N,Y with DBR $01 or $81). The type number comes from a placement row (+3, the PlacementAaaSss lists) or from a lair record (+$15, LairRecords).

=== ENTRY LAYOUT (14 bytes) ===
+0 attack, +1 defence, +2 HP (a binary byte), +3 word EXP (BCD), +5 animation id, +6 word flags (becomes $16; $8000 is added at spawn), +8 word animation table, +A animation bank, +B word script, +D script bank. +8..+A is the 3-byte Address field of structs.json and +B..+D the @Code field. Damage (comments in the combat code): the player's hit on a monster is max(1, attack_current - monster defence (+1)); a monster's hit on the player is attack (+0) - 1 - defense_current, at least 0. The EXP word is added in BCD by KillTarget and drawn as digits by RunEnemyDeath.
HP is binary and EXP is BCD: the bestiary values of docs/walkthrough/enemy-bestiary.md match this reading for every enemy that could be matched (for example Metal Mantis 50 HP and 50 EXP = bytes $32 and $0050).

=== WHAT THE OPERANDS SAY ===
Animation table (+8..+A): 358 of the 469 entries use $7E3800 (the sprite map the scene loader expanded into WRAM: the step lists of ordinary actors travel with the scene), 69 use PaletteAnimLists (bank $0D, the colour animations: mostly types $01-$0F of every list, 14, 14, 13, 15, 5, 3 and 5 types in worlds 0-6; none of the enemies), 7 use PlayerAnims (entry 0 of every world, the hero), 4 use EffectAnims and 31 have $000000 (the actor selects its own table with COP A8). Flags word (+6): $2010 95 times, $2040 87, $0040 49, $0000 43, $2048 39, $2050 38, $1000 22, $3040 21 and 28 more values with fewer entries.
Entry 0 of every list is the hero: attack 1, defence 2, HP 3, animation 0, flags $1180, table PlayerAnims, script InitPlayerActor. The seven copies are identical (the stats are not used; the player's own stats live in the $1B.. fields).

=== ENEMY TYPES (matched by stats) ===
The ROM names nothing. The part notes of the seven lists name the enemy types by matching HP and EXP against the walkthrough bestiary (inferred). Where the bestiary gives several enemies the same stats the ids cannot be told apart this way and the note says so. The four bosses whose ROM HP differs from the bestiary, the world 6 Purple Bull and the types that match no bestiary row are OQ-I033-1 to OQ-I033-4.
